items_missed: 1_set_agenda: Never asked 'How are you today?' and didn't check move-date availability until the booking step at the very end instead of up front.
2_probe: Never asked about storage or storage stops.
5_estimate: Didn't use a relatable equivalent (e.g., a school-bus or truck-load comparison) to help the customer picture the time/volume.

6_save_your_ass: No prep speech at all — never told the customer that prepping before move day shortens the move and lowers the bill, no consolidation examples (toys, drawers, garden tools), no 'take a carload' tip.
7_quote_booking: Never mentioned business hours or how to reach Einstein Moving with questions before the move.

8_politeness: Used the customer's name correctly only twice (opening ID check, closing name/phone verification) and then got it wrong at the very end — 'have a great day Brian' when the customer is Ryan.
9_bonus: No rapport-building moment or humor beyond scripted affirmations, and didn't pair the No Worries $2,000 coverage with the standard baseline (60 cents/lb) valuation explanation.
top_strength: Nicole nailed the full pricing and differentiators section (20/20) — rate, what's included, No Worries coverage, Meet Your Mover, On-Time Guarantee, and the full no-hidden-fees pitch all landed cleanly. She also handled two curveballs well: when Ryan said 'we really only need Einstein movers for the furniture and like the odd items,' she caught the no-boxes change immediately and recalculated the estimate live, and when he mentioned an emailed inventory list and a pre-existing damage spot on a dresser, she found the email on the spot and reassured him proactively about photo documentation.
coaching_note: The Save Your Ass section is a total zero here — this is the highest-value section for controlling move time and Nicole skipped it entirely. Once she gets to the estimate, she needs to tell the customer straight: pack ahead of time and consolidate loose stuff (drawers, garage items, anything small) into fewer piles or your own car, and that shortens the clock and lowers the final bill. Also, double check names before you hang up — closing a call by calling the customer 'Brian' when his name is Ryan undercuts an otherwise strong, attentive call. Small fix, worth tightening.
phone_presence_notes: Polite and consistently affirming ('Awesome,' 'Thank you so much for mentioning that'), but the warmth reads formulaic and repeated rather than adaptive, and misnaming the customer at the close undercuts genuine attentiveness.
